hot.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
hot.summary: Projection sampling transforms expert demonstrations into responses more like those of a pretrained model before standard supervised fine-tuning, using the model to propose continuations and an MCMC procedure to select them. On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, it raises SciKnowEval Chemistry L-3 single-shot accuracy to 66.0%, while the five-task prior-capability average is 58.6%, below the base model’s 59.7%.

hot.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
hot.summary: VISTA gives a multimodal model access to archived game frames, allowing it to retrieve earlier images, compare moments, and enlarge details while reasoning in language and choosing actions. Across 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, Claude Opus 5.0 completes all games with a mean Relative Human Action Efficiency score of 100.00, using 7,302 actions versus 17,135 for first-time humans. This public-set result does not establish performance on unseen games.

hot.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
hot.summary: The paper trains a looped language model to settle toward fixed points across repeated applications of a shared block. Terminal key-value (KV) sharing retains only final cache banks; separate methods reuse endpoints for prefill and reinforcement learning. At 1.6B parameters, the learned-depth-prior model scores 60.00% on the downstream average with four rather than twelve KV banks, in the reported setup.

hot.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
hot.summary: ScholarCatalyst benchmarks whether systems can retrieve prior papers that project authors judged helpful or potentially helpful to early-stage research. It uses 894 retrospectively annotated queries from 207 computer-science projects, with author-labeled positives and hard negatives. Across its reported settings, agentic search reaches overall Recall@20 of 0.42 versus 0.48 for embedding retrieval, measuring retrospective judgments rather than successful inspiration.

hot.title: Looped Diffusion Transformer
hot.summary: Looped-DiT improves text-to-image generation by repeating shared middle Transformer blocks within each denoising step, refining hidden representations without adding unique parameters. Deep Supervision trains intermediate predictions, and Self-Modulating Attention regulates repeated updates. Its B/16 model averages 71.5 across six benchmarks versus 69.0 for 1.7B InternVL-U, at 150 versus 732 TFLOPs per image, in 260M-parameter pixel-space models using 512 × 512 resolution.

hot.title: Recent Advanced Technologies in Financial Time-Series Generation: A Survey
hot.summary: The survey organizes financial time-series generation by task and technique. It distinguishes extrapolation, which extends an observed sequence, imputation, which fills gaps using context on both sides, and synthesis, which creates new sequences. It also maps methods and public data resources and identifies open challenges. Its contribution is a research taxonomy, not comparative evidence that any method performs better.

hot.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
hot.summary: RPG lets robot skills improve through practice without changing model weights. It revises reusable executable skills and system prompts using failure diagnosis, then validates candidate and merged changes across tasks. In simulation, held-out success across 22 manipulation tasks rose from 63/220 (28.6%) after round 1 to 209/220 (95.0%) after round 15; this is not matched-compute evidence.

hot.title: Conditionals, Couplings and Toric Geometry: Established Results and a Fukaya Programme
hot.summary: The paper studies the geometry of joint distributions with marginals. It represents compatible tables as a coupling polytope and proves that under a nondegeneracy condition it is Delzant. When every cell inequality defines a facet, the product coupling is the unique critical point of the symplectic potential. In the monotone uniform 2×3 case, imported Floer theory singles out its fibre.

hot.title: SkillRefiner: Offline Skill Refinement from Historical Agent Traces
hot.summary: SKILLREFINER refines an agent’s reusable instructions from traces and feedback without generating new executions during refinement. It summarizes and clusters runs by outcome, proposes edits, and checks failure-derived edits against evidence before merging. On 200 held-out SpreadsheetBench tasks, it reached 84.0% accuracy versus 79.0% for Trace2Skill and 78.5% for GEPA; token comparisons exclude collection costs and do not establish computation.

hot.title: World Motion Models: Flexible Sequence Modeling of SE(3) Trajectories
hot.summary: World Motion Models (WMMs) represent moving entities as time sequences of rigid poses, with features identifying entity types. By assigning each pose its own noise level, a model can generate unknown poses conditioned on known poses, supporting varied motion tasks. On Language Table, WMM’s macro-average success is 87.2%, versus 80.0% for LCB; results use separate checkpoints per benchmark.

hot.title: Sphere Encoder 2
hot.summary: Sphere Encoder 2 generates images by decoding random points on a sphere, with a training path that separates reconstruction from generation. It rotates encoded latents from 0° to 90° and applies score-matching and semantic losses near the equator, alongside reconstruction losses at low angles. On ImageNet at 256 × 256, it reports FDr6 4.92 using 23 times less sampling compute than PixNerd-XL, but higher gFID.

hot.title: Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free
hot.summary: LoopCD guides looped Transformers by extrapolating from an earlier prediction toward the final prediction for the same prefix, without adding recurrent iterations. It offers logits and hidden-state variants, with hidden-state guidance avoiding an extra output pass. On AIME 2024, adaptive LoopCD-Logits raises Ouro-2.6B-Thinking pass@1 from 61.88% to 73.33%; results are not uniformly positive across tasks and metrics.

hot.title: Sharpening Tax in Post-Training
hot.summary: The authors compare base and post-trained agents on three agentic benchmarks across repeated rollouts, and introduce Sharpening Tax to measure how much success retries recover. For Gemma-4-31B on WebShop, the harness-equipped base model rises from 22.7% pass@1 to 87.6% pass@128, while its post-trained counterpart reaches 39.5% and 56.0%. The comparison is observational and varies by model scale and rollout budget.

hot.title: Precise Attribution of Model Interventions: Attribution Sets, Mechanism Reach and Path Defects
hot.summary: The paper develops a provenance calculus that represents explanations of model changes as sets and uses linear programming to measure uncertainty and test intervention reach. Under an exact KL-regularized optimizer and bounded rewards, RLHF output changes form a polytope. In a synthetic example, a drifted change has residual 0.1934; conclusions apply to finite probes and declared mechanisms, not hidden causes.

hot.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
hot.summary: AutoCompact trains coding agents to compact history proactively, preserving findings, workspace state, and next actions while discarding exploration. It learns when to compact, what to summarize, and how to continue through demonstrations and reinforcement learning. With the model and scaffold, it achieves 39.6% on SWE-bench Verified versus 30.4% for Base; benefits also appear at 256K without reaching the compaction threshold.

hot.title: SPEEDRUNBENCH: Challenging LLM Agents With Video Game Speedrunning
hot.summary: SPEEDRUNBENCH tests whether agents can find faster routes across nine games. Agents play from screenshots or edit complete action traces, starting from a supplied route or from scratch. In a controlled SuperTux test, DeepSeek-V4-Pro reduced its route from 9,428 to 1,847 frames with up to 200 candidate evaluations per turn. No agent reached a human record under the practical budget.

hot.title: Mastering Atari 2600 Games with Discovered Options
hot.summary: Wayfarer lets an Atari agent learn multi-step options online and choose among them alongside primitive actions, using a learned Laplacian representation to shape skills and task-value learning to select them. On ten challenging Atari games, it reaches a median human-normalized score of 0.69 after 200 million frames, but this aggregate result does not establish universal dominance or faster training.

hot.title: Non-Equilibrium Dissipative Morphogenesis in an Anhydrous Enstatite-Rich Nebular Pebble Matrix: Evidence from Organic-Mineral Textures and Stable Isotopes
hot.summary: The authors interpret a mineral fragment’s biomorphic textures as abiotic patterns formed through physical and chemical processes. They report bulk carbon of 16.8422 weight percent in unacidified material, and a cellular network with coefficient of variation about 8.4% and mean junction coordination of 5.92, near six for ideal hexagons. These observations motivate, but do not establish, the mechanism or provenance.

hot.title: OneStreamer: Unifying Perception, Memory, and Proactive Response in Streaming Video Interaction
hot.summary: OneStreamer addresses streaming video questions by retaining generated, time-grounded captions alongside a recent visual window and producing responses when its control state calls for them. In a controlled comparison using the same checkpoint and Recent-16 window, caption memory raises OVOBench-Backward ASI from 63.5 to 71.6, while real-time scores also rise. The results support these benefits in tested settings, not universally.

hot.title: MoSE3: Learning World-Space SE(3) at Every Pixel
hot.summary: MoSE3 predicts per-pixel rotation and translation from monocular video by combining dense 3D point tracks with learned rigidity embeddings. A differentiable weighted Horn fit uses embedding-based grouping to recover transforms in a shared world frame. On iTACO, it reports 12.30° mean relative rotation error, compared with 28.07° for Track4World-Pi3x; this result is limited to synthetic articulated-object evaluation.

likes.title: Tokenization: A Survey for Modern NLP
likes.summary: Tokenization is presented as a core language-model design choice that shapes sequence length, computational cost, multilingual equity, evaluation, and security—not merely as preprocessing. The survey reviews established subword methods and emerging byte-level, latent, and visual alternatives, finding that BPE still dominates practice while no tokenizer consistently optimizes compression, linguistic alignment, downstream quality, and crosslingual fairness at once.

likes.title: Context Language Models
likes.summary: Context Language Models let an agent edit its live conversation by mirroring the transcript into a file whose changes synchronize with subsequent model calls. The approach supports multiple agents and zero-shot context management. On BrowseComp-Plus, Qwen3.6-27B reached 59.4% accuracy, with 21.5% fewer prefix-reuse FLOPs than Codex-style summarization. Results vary by setting and do not isolate editing alone.

likes.title: Invent a Dataset: Measuring Dataset Generation Abilities with Zero Seed Data

The prompt-based API is evaluated on eight requests using quality, semantic diversity, and downstream fine-tuning tests. At 5,000 samples, it scores 7.90 versus 6.76 for Claude Opus 5; at 20,000, diversity is 37% higher than GLM-5.3, but results do not establish universal capability.

likes.summary: Google DeepMind announces Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier model built to sustain deep reasoning across long, multi-step workflows in software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity defense. Argon is first rolling out to trusted cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program, with broader API and consumer access to follow after safeguards are strengthened. It launches at an introductory price of $2 / $10 per million input / output tokens.

likes.title: Simplex Diffusion Models
likes.summary: Simplex Diffusion Models (SDMs) generate sequences while retaining token uncertainty as a probability vector instead of making a categorical choice. They use closed-form transitions with churn rather than ODE integration. On TinyGSM, SDM reaches 49.0% versus 45.8% for masked diffusion at 512 evaluations; after distillation, it reaches 32.1% at 8 versus 21.4% at 128. These results come from small models and do not establish general superiority.

likes.title: Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning
likes.summary: APPL carries each skill’s structural prior into runtime selection, preserving prior-specific policies, handoff conditions, support, and verification evidence. A construction agent builds and checks policies, while a runtime agent selects one and its execution conditions. With two demonstrations per task, APPL reached 89.58% macro OOD success across six MetaWorld tasks. Results are simulated, and priors do not guarantee competence.

likes.title: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
likes.summary: MatToolBench evaluates whether agents can complete materials-science workflows across specialist software, scripts, and scientific databases. It includes 204 tasks on 10 tools, with GUI, hybrid OriginPro, code, and diagnostic mixed tasks, and scores partial criteria separately from complete success. GPT-5.4 reaches a 45.0% code success rate, while Claude-sonnet-4.6 reaches 25.0% for GUI tasks; these results do not establish readiness for unsupervised use.

likes.title: DexAgent: An Agentic Human2Sim2Robot Framework for Dexterous Manipulation with Self-Evolving Tool Library
likes.summary: DexAgent converts one egocentric RGB video and a task prompt into robot-training data by adapting reconstruction, motion skills, and property-specific verifiers to each task. It refines subgoals, varies simulated starting states, and renders observations for rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Across eleven tasks, policies averaged 63.6% success versus 18.2% for SPIDER, but verification does not eliminate errors or establish causation.

likes.title: Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation
likes.summary: The paper trains a proposer to revise a language-model agent’s executable harness—its workflow for model calls, tools, and information flow—using execution outcomes, while keeping the solver fixed. At test time, frozen proposer and solver weights support successive harness edits. On 21 unseen reasoning families, mean held-out score rises from 0.32 to 0.62, but five harder families are excluded.

likes.title: T$^2$Mem: Learning Test-Time Memory for Robotics
likes.summary: T²Mem gives a vision-language-action robot policy a fixed-size episodic memory in fast weights updated during deployment, while learned policy parameters remain fixed. At each observation, a learned interface writes and reads compact vision-language associations for action selection. On RoboMME, it achieves 56.83% macro-averaged terminal success across 16 tasks, versus 17.93% for memory-free π0.5, but the result is benchmark-specific.

likes.title: Hard Vision, Easy Vision: What GPT-6 Astra Reveals Across Computer Vision
likes.summary: The authors evaluate six general-purpose vision systems across 34 capabilities, 55 benchmarks, and nine areas, comparing outputs with specialists and human references where available. GPT-6 Astra reaches 89.1 F1 at IoU 0.5 in 2D detection, versus 78.4 for Rex-Omni, but generalists score 17.2–17.7 dB PSNR in restoration versus MIRAGE’s 30.7, revealing limits in faithful reconstruction and metric precision.

likes.title: Improving Test-Time Scaling with Adaptive Looped Transformers
likes.summary: TaH2 adaptively loops shared Transformer layers in latent space, deciding token by token whether another pass is worth taking from measured next-token loss gains. On post-trained 1.7B Qwen3 models, it reaches 2.74 AIME accuracy points per doubling of decoding FLOPs versus 1.79 for Standard, and 15.4% versus 12.0% at matched compute. It does not reduce reported decoding cost or latency.
